question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 64, 11, 66, 98, 25, 17, 50, 75 and 62 is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the Assumed Mean Method (Deviation Method) for faster calculation.

Let the assumed mean = 50.

Sum of deviations = (+14) + (−39) + (+16) + (+48) + (−25) + (−33) + 0 + (+25) + (+12) = +18

Average deviation = +18 ÷ 9 = +2

Actual Mean = 50 + 2 = 52

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 64, 11, 66, 98, 25, 17, 50, 75, 62

Total number of observations (n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 64 + 11 + 66 + 98 + 25 + 17 + 50 + 75 + 62

⇒ Sum = 468

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 468 ÷ 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 52

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Assumed Mean Method

Mean = Assumed Mean + (Sum of deviations ÷ Number of observations). This is highly effective to simplify manual addition of large or complex numbers.

Weighted Average

When values appear with different frequencies or given weights, Mean = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

Combined Mean

If two distinct groups have individual means A₁ and A₂ with n₁ and n₂ number of elements, Combined Mean = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
